chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The qasāmah was only instituted so that the matter may be made weightier thereby against a man known for concealment who is accused; so if they testify against him, their testimony is admissible."

key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُمْ: their testimony; their legal witness statement
key_terms.لِيُغَلَّظَ: to make weightier or more severe in legal force
key_terms.ٱلرَّجُلِ: the man; the accused male individual in the case
key_terms.ٱلْقَسَامَةُ: qasāmah; a legal procedure involving oaths in cases of accusation
key_terms.ٱلْمَعْرُوفِ بِٱلسِّتْرِ: known for concealment; a person characterized by secrecy or hidden conduct

ai.seo_question: Why was qasāmah instituted in Islamic law, and when is testimony accepted against an accused person?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal function of qasāmah as a means of intensifying evidentiary consideration in the case of an accused person known for concealment. It indicates that when witnesses testify against such a person, their testimony is accepted within this judicial context.
